clue.text: Restrains urges to drink, first and foremost

indicators.note: says the drink piece is placed at the very front, ahead of the urges

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
presses means urges or pushes someone

explanation.surface: Someone holds back their cravings for alcohol above all else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and foremost' reads like an emphatic sign-off to the surface, but it is a placing instruction for the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress something is to hold it back or restrain it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One cheers up after second drink

indicators.note: puts the up piece behind the second piece in the answer

parts.note: taken as written
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A drinker raises a glass after a second pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One cheers up' looks like someone being comforted; split it so 'up' becomes wordplay and 'One cheers' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter is a fan who cheers a team on, so one who cheers fits.

clue.text: Exercises a great deal, gripping a kind of bar?

indicators.note: something gripping another holds it inside, so the bar goes within

parts.note: piles means a great deal, a lot
T as in a T-bar, a bar shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A gym-goer works out hard, holding on to some sort of bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts A and T (a T-bar) inside PILES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a system of body-conditioning exercises, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Commemorative bookplate is given to old party member finally

indicators.note: says the word is is attached on the end of what comes before

parts.note: ex means former or old
Lib is short for Liberal, a political party

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word member

explanation.surface: A memorial plate is presented to a former party member at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from 'member'; 'given to' puts IS at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex libris, Latin for from the books of, is printed on a plate marking a book's owner.

clue.text: Clearly reveal intention to start working in the market?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for making plain what you plan to do

definitions.text: to start working in the market?
definitions.meaning: literally, a trader laying out goods on a market stall

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make one's aims plain, from the literal act of a trader displaying wares.

clue.text: Presumably one will find religious adherent talking with queen

indicators.note: says the word is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a Sikh is a follower of Sikhism
ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A believer chats with a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' turns SIKH into its sound-alike SEEK; ER is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: One who seeks presumably finds, as in seek and ye shall find; a whimsical description.

clue.text: Avocado and vegetable ratatouille for starters

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: for starters points to the opening letter of ratatouille

explanation.surface: A menu offers avocado and vegetable stew as first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' gives R, the first letter of 'ratatouille'.
explanation.definitionFit: An avocado is also called an avocado pear, so the fruit name serves.

clue.text: Severely criticise everyone in court over role

indicators.note: over means turned back to front, so the first two pieces read backwards as one run

parts.note: all means everyone
up means appearing in court, as in up before the magistrate
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: A judge harshly attacks everybody in court for their part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ALLUP into PULLA; PART follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull apart a piece of work is an idiom for criticising it savagely.

clue.text: Is not speaking informally on English course

parts.note: ain't is the casual spoken form of is not
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone talks slangily about an English topic.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a racecourse, an example of a course for horse racing.

clue.text: Good fortune to go to college offering many languages

indicators.note: says the good-fortune pieces follow on after the college

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a kind of college
lot means fortune or fate

explanation.surface: A student lucky enough to go to college finds a wide range of language courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go to' is placing the luck behind the college; poly was the common name for a British polytechnic.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot speaker or text uses several languages; the adjective matches.

clue.text: District of London is getting better for some of its residents?

indicators.note: suggests the local way of speaking, dropping the opening aitch

parts.note: healing means getting better

explanation.surface: A London neighbourhood is improving, at least for some who live there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for some of its residents' points to Cockney h-dropping: HEALING said without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing is a borough in west London, an example of a district there.

clue.text: Pledge made solemnly is old hat, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the word hat turns up in an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: A solemn promise is described as stale, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' scrambles only the three letters of the headwear, not the whole phrase 'old hat'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise or vow, a direct synonym.

clue.text: I read a blue version of this French poet

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader tries a risqué edition of a French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges IREADABLUE; 'blue' hints at the poet's scandalous Les Fleurs du mal.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Baudelaire was a nineteenth-century French poet, author of Les Fleurs du mal.

clue.text: Airman, one getting stuck in river bed

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England

indicators.note: the one piece is pushed inside the bed piece

parts.note: a plot is a garden bed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A flier gets trapped in a riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stuck in' puts I inside PLOT; the Test is a Hampshire chalk-stream river.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot is an airman who flies new aircraft to try them out.

clue.text: Like schoolmasters, they are involved with small class

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together into a new order

parts.note: CL is the abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: Teachers are busy with a small group of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' rearranges THEYARE plus CL.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacherly is an adjective meaning in the manner of a teacher, matching like schoolmasters.

clue.text: City, part of colossal empire

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A city forms a portion of a vast imperial realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' points into 'colossal empire'.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem is a city, in Massachusetts and Oregon among other places.

clue.text: Skill needed, working within religious community

indicators.note: puts the working piece inside the skill piece

parts.note: mastery means great skill
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: Expertise is required when working inside a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' signals the container; 'needed' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery houses a community of monks living under religious vows.

clue.text: Hot dish boy served up: duck in wine

indicators.note: says those pieces go inside the wine

parts.note: vino is informal for wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A waiter brings a dish of duck cooked in wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns LAD into DAL; DAL and O (a duck) go 'in' VINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a very hot curry, a fiery dish.

clue.text: Artillery strike on North African capital

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
to bat is to hit or strike

explanation.surface: Guns bombard an African capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is a British Army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco in North Africa.

clue.text: Sailor, say, is a neighbourly sort?

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A seaman is asked whether he is a friendly type.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a standard crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutter is one whose property borders another's, so a neighbour in a literal sense.

clue.text: Representation of epistle, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: says the epistle piece goes inside the manner of speaking

parts.note: diction is a style of speaking
Ep. is the abbreviation for epistle

explanation.surface: Someone describes a letter in a certain way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'a manner of speaking' is a synonym, not a homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction is a portrayal or representation of something.

clue.text: US state document causes animesity

parts.note: Ill. is the abbreviation for Illinois
a will is a legal document

explanation.surface: An American state paper stirs up hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL. is the abbreviation for Illinois; the page scan prints animosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility toward someone; the held text spells animosity as animesity.

clue.text: Swiss dramatist has day at school

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday

explanation.surface: A Swiss playwright spends a day in class.
explanation.walkthrough: Max Frisch wrote The Fire Raisers and Andorra.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Frisch was a Swiss playwright and novelist.

clue.text: Writer does editorial work, as approved

parts.note: an author is a writer
read as is ed, that is, is the editor

explanation.surface: An author edits a text and gives it the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does editorial work' is read as 'is ED', ED being short for editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorised means officially approved or sanctioned.

clue.text: Being rich mostly is an advantage

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: plush means rich or luxurious

explanation.surface: Being wealthy is largely a benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of PLUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a benefit or advantage, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Keeps one out of newspaper articles?

indicators.note: out of says one piece is removed from the articles

parts.note: stories are newspaper articles
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone holds back one of the newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes I from STORIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To store something is to keep it, so stores means keeps.

clue.text: Pimento, ultimately essential ingredient in special stew

indicators.note: the selected letter becomes an ingredient inside the mixture
stew implies the letters are stirred together into a new order
ultimately points to the closing letter of essential

explanation.surface: Allspice is the key ingredient in a special stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives L from 'essential'; 'stew' rearranges SPECIAL to ALSPICE; 'ingredient in' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is another name for allspice, the dried berry of a Caribbean tree.

clue.text: Ingratiating sergeant major leaves the military

indicators.note: leaves means the officer departs, so those letters are removed

parts.note: smarmy means ingratiating or oily

explanation.surface: A fawning NCO quits the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes SM from SMARMY.
explanation.definitionFit: The army is the land fighting force, a branch of the military.

clue.text: Fellow left money gets to act in a musical

parts.note: he stands for a man or fellow

indicators.note: gets means takes in, so the act piece goes inside the money

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
to do is to act

explanation.surface: A man who left some cash is cast in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' means takes in, signalling the container; lolly is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello, Dolly! is a Broadway musical by Jerry Herman.
